summary: Gatineau Park, Pontiac, QC: wooden-cab fire tower on steel legs, built 1940, still standing but weathered; NCC says not open to public; NHLR-registered 2022.

facts.design: Wooden cab on steel support beams, similar to other metal fire lookouts such as the Aermotor LS-40; small exterior balcony
facts.agency: Ministère des Forêts, de la Faune et des Parcs (administrator per NHLR); National Capital Commission (cooperator per NHLR; manages Gatineau Park per NCC)

staffing.as_of: undated (NCC page says forest rangers used the tower in the past)

access.note: NCC says the tower is not accessible to the public; the trail passes it and closes in winter

visit.trail_note: 4.2 km loop with 300 m of climbing up the Eardley Escarpment (Chute-de-Luskville trail); two viewpoints and the tower are on the trail; closed in winter

events.note: Built in 1940 (NCC French page; NHLR 'Built' field also gives 1940)
Date registered December 25, 2022; nominated by William Haddad

notes_for_editor: Brief has no local_unit; the story uses the municipality of Pontiac, which the NCC page names. NHLR gives 'Gatineau Park' as location and the NCC page gives the western sector of the park. The 1940 build year agrees across NHLR and NCC. No fire history, restoration or dated staffing record was found, so none is stated. Three sources read; the NHLR photo is credited to William Haddad but no photo URL was captured. A search hit for the 'Gatineau Ridge Road to the Fire Tower' trail is near Chelsea, not Luskville, and was not used.
